description: Steady C1 content batch for The Sound Maze. Each target is spoken aloud; the learner selects its spelling. Draft content is not wired into the live game.

questions.explain: Stagnant has /æ/ in its stressed first syllable. Statement has /eɪ/, stinging has /ɪ/, and stunning has /ʌ/.
Cumbersome begins with /ʌ/. Customary also begins with /ʌ/, while cosmetic begins with /ɑ/ and cement with /ɪ/.
Diligence begins with /ɪ/ in its first syllable. Delegate begins with /ɛ/, dalliance with /æ/, and dollop with /ɑ/.
Ptarmigan begins with /t/ because the initial p is silent. Pivotal begins with /p/, theoretical with /θ/, and gnawing with /n/.
Tsunami begins with /s/ in standard General American pronunciation; the initial t is silent. Zoology begins with /z/, while safari and ceramic begin with /s/ but have different following sounds.
Hierarchy begins with /h/ in careful General American pronunciation. Irony begins with a vowel, rhetoric with /r/, and eulogy with /j/.
Drought ends with /t/. Drown ends with /n/, drowsy with /zi/, and drowned with /nd/.
Scratched ends with /tʃt/. Scratch ends with /tʃ/, scratches with /ɪz/, and scratching with /ɪŋ/.
Risks ends with /sks/. Risk ends with /sk/, risky with /i/, and risen with /ən/.
Supersession is pronounced /ˌsuːpərˈsɛʃən/. The alternatives have different stressed vowels or consonant sequences.
Belligerent has a soft g pronounced /dʒ/ and a distinctive /ˈbɛlɪdʒərənt/ sequence. The other choices differ in their medial consonants and vowel patterns.
Miscellaneous is pronounced /ˌmɪsəˈleɪniəs/. The alternatives have different syllable counts, stress, and vowel sequences.
